Dear /v/Gaming,

As some of you may know, I run a long-form weekly game news show; while it runs on Youtube, it also goes on television on VOD on a channel called 9 Bit as well as through Soul of the South- I'm also working on bringing the show to Verizon Fios (hence why it's 23 minutes every week!). For next week's episode I'll be talking about the localization of Fire Emblem Fates and the importance of a true translation, and if things should be changed to suit local tastes.

I'm inviting you guys to weigh in in the comments below to let me know what you think about the subject, if you're a disappointed Fire Emblem fan, etc. I'll be sharing the most insightful comments on my show this week!

Also, if you have any non-Voat friends who prefer to use Twitter, this should contact us here.
Let's talk about localization and Fire Emblem on television.

I'm always impressed with how consistently you engage with /v/gaming and on Voat as a whole, /u/Jourdy288. If all content creators participated like you do, we wouldn't even need a content creator policy. I haven't played any Fire Emblem games (I just bought Awakening to try it out) but I wanted to give you kudos for being a part of the community.

On the hand, there is a long history of references to alcohol, religion and violence being censored in localization back in the NES and SNES days. And we always look back on it with an air of "Those wacky fundamentalist christians in the 80's and 90's" But for all these superficial changes, I think we mostly got the essence of the game fine. Nobody is still grousing over pubs being changed to cafes, or the red cross signs being taken off of hospitals.

Now SJWs are getting games censored. Maybe it's something small like a butt slap or a costume. And like the changes in the NES/SNES era, I think we'll look back on it as a goofy trivial change that was unnecessary, but thankfully left the essence of the game in tact.

I'm really not sure the same could be said about Fire Emblem Fates. The localization process has been so much more invasive, and appears to have changed the essential nature of numerous characters. Presumably the overall story remains unchanged though? But if the rumors I've heard about large portions of dialog being cut entirely, it's hard to imagine a game can lose that much writing and not lose a good portion of the story's nuance and richness.

It's not that I don't get where the translators for Fire Emblem Fates are coming from. I used to watch a lot of fansubbed anime, and still read a bit of manga here and there, and you routinely see translators struggling with how to translate deep rooted cultural references, or japanese language puns. Then there are games like Elite Beat Agents where all they could bring over from the Japanese original was the theme and the mechanics, but aside from that it's a totally different game.

Regardless of all that though, it still seems to me that the company that localized Fire Emblem Fates seriously dropped the ball, and went too far in trying to localize not just the language and culture, but also the morality.
